answer.rationale: Verified memory_b1 confirms that rolling back a bad release cleared a checkout error spike with no customer impact. Verified memory_b5 confirms that routing report queries to read replicas can relieve primary write-path pressure, but that is a secondary optimization rather than an acute fix. Current signals (p99 climbing for 90 minutes, release 2 hours ago, write path at 5x target during peak settlement) match the pattern in memory_b1 where a recent release degraded the write path and rollback was the fastest safe resolution. Add_capacity or route_read_replicas would take longer to take effect and do not address the likely root cause. Regional_failover is unnecessary because there is no regional degradation signal. Enable_circuit_breaker protects against partner outages, not self-inflicted latency regressions. One intervention: roll back the release.
